summary_paragraph: A woman with prior bariatric surgery and a gastrostomy tube was admitted to the surgery service for a persistently draining, non-healing upper midline abdominal wound after recent open gastrostomy tube placement. She underwent reopening and debridement of the abdominal wound with removal of a retained suture/foreign body, then recovered overnight with stable vital signs and no fever, pain controlled on oral medication, and stable cardiopulmonary status. Her diet was advanced and tube feeds were resumed and tolerated with stable blood glucose levels. She was discharged home with services on oral amoxicillin-clavulanate for 7 days, instructions for twice-daily wound packing/dressing changes, and surgical clinic follow-up.
problems: Other specified complications of procedures not elsewhere classified
Surgical operation with formation of external stoma causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
